rationale: M60 php round — the RECEIVER OWNER, at all six member-position emission sites. A member is PUBLISHED as (bare name, ownerName) and the EDGE carried no owner, so `$this->render()`, `self::render()`, `parent::render()` and `Widget::render()` published the same target string and were mutually indistinguishable; `render` is a method on many classes, so the reverse walk picked one declaration by a rule nobody chose. The receiver node was on hand at every emission site and was discarded. `expectRelationships` pins the owner per receiver shape, and — the half that matters more — `meta.owner: null` pins the THREE shapes where no owner may appear: a plain-variable receiver (a), a chained receiver `$this->svc->m()` (b), and `parent::` in a class with NO base clause (c). Those guard the expensive direction, where a wrong owner sends a reverse walk to a real method on the WRONG class and becomes wrong refactoring advice rather than a missing edge. A fourth case is pinned separately and is NOT a no-owner case: `External extends DeclaredInAnotherFile` DOES declare a base, so the owner is that name, which this file does not publish — right and unresolved, and collapsing it into (c) would make a rule that is merely incomplete look like one that invents. `self::class` is pinned as `uses`-absent because a class_constant_access naming `class` is the `::class` keyword, not a member. The pins are hand-written from the grammar, not dumped from a run: the receiver classification reads node types and FIELD names only (`scoped_property_access_expression` has [scope] and [name]; `class_constant_access_expression` has NO field names and is read positionally, both probed against the pinned grammar).

expectRelationships.note: The ONLY edge to this target comes from `\Fixture\ReceiverOwner\Qualified::onlyViaAbsolutePath()`, so this row pins the reduction of a qualified scope to its LEAF name. With only the unqualified twin present the row would be satisfied by it and the reduction would go unpinned, because a fixture row matches with some().
Property syntax does not name the viaThis method; retain the read without qualifying it to that declaration.

forbidRelationships.note: `self::class` is the ::class KEYWORD, not a member. The existing rule skips it; this row stops an owner rule that reads the node from attaching an owner to it.
